title: Working with Remote Patches
execute:
  warning: false
---

DASCore reads remote resources through [`UPath`](https://pypi.org/project/universal-pathlib/); tested backends include `memory://`, `s3://`, and `http://`.

| Operation | Default behavior |
|---|---|
| `scan`, `get_format` | Avoid downloading a complete file |
| `scan_payloads` | Same cache policy, but may transfer and retain full coordinate arrays; prefer `scan` or `scan_to_df` for broad listings |
| `read`, spool indexing/iteration | Perform the heavier I/O needed to load data |

# Basic example

`memory://` demonstrates the remote interface without network access:

```{python}
from upath import UPath

import dascore as dc

remote_path = UPath("memory://dascore/tutorial/remote_patch.h5")
dc.write(dc.get_example_patch(), remote_path, "DASDAE")

summary = dc.scan(remote_path)[0]
payload = dc.scan_payloads(remote_path, snap=False)[0]
loaded = dc.read(remote_path)[0]
spool = dc.spool(remote_path)
```

The summary holds compact coordinate envelopes and source fields, the payload holds the format's full coordinate manager, and indexing the spool loads the patch array. Backends that support direct access may need no local cached copy.

# Cache policy

These `dascore.config` settings control remote caching:

| Setting | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `remote_cache_dir` | Directory for materialized remote files; must be private to the current user |
| `allow_remote_cache` | Permit caching for data reads |
| `allow_remote_cache_for_metadata` | Permit caching for metadata operations |
| `warn_on_remote_cache` | Warn on the first download into the cache |

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import mkdtemp

from dascore.config import config_context

with config_context(
    remote_cache_dir=Path(mkdtemp()),
    allow_remote_cache=True,
    allow_remote_cache_for_metadata=False,
):
    patch = dc.read(remote_path)[0]
```

When a metadata query needs a full download and metadata caching is off, DASCore raises [`RemoteCacheError`](`dascore.exceptions.RemoteCacheError`). Format detection skips a reader that would need the download and raises only if no other reader claims the file. Detection reads only the header bytes of MiniSEED and SEG-Y files, but SEG-Y's binary header sits past the first block, so on a server without byte-range support its detection also needs the opt-in. Scanning or reading either format needs a local copy, which a scan makes only after the opt-in. Opt in only for a known operation:

```python
http_path = UPath("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dasdae/test_data/master/das/example_dasdae_event_1.h5")

with config_context(allow_remote_cache_for_metadata=True):
    summary = dc.scan(http_path)[0]
```

Once per session, a cached copy is checked against the remote's size and version fields (such as `ETag`) and downloaded again if the remote changed. Offline, the copy is kept; a remote that is gone or forbidden is never read from the cache.

# Reads and spools

`dc.read(...)` may download a remote file when `allow_remote_cache=True`. A spool's `get_contents()` uses only metadata, while indexing and iteration load data. If a backend cannot provide spool metadata directly, enable metadata caching.

```python
remote_spool = dc.spool(http_path)
metadata = remote_spool.get_contents()
with config_context(allow_remote_cache=True):
    patch = remote_spool[0]
```

# Remote HDF5 and garbage collection

Remote HDF5 reads can deadlock if cyclic garbage collection runs on fsspec's event-loop thread while h5py holds its global lock (see [h5py's file-like object documentation](https://docs.h5py.org/en/stable/high/file.html#python-file-like-objects)). DASCore therefore pauses cyclic garbage collection while remote HDF5 handles are open, restores it when the last one closes, and warns once per process. Only cyclic garbage accumulates meanwhile; reference counting still frees objects immediately, and local reads are unaffected. To silence the warning:

```python
with config_context(warn_on_gc_pause=False):
    patch = dc.read(http_path)[0]
```

# Transfer tuning

Two settings control the remote HDF5 block cache:

| Setting | Default | Trade-off |
|---|---:|---|
| `remote_hdf5_block_size` | 5 MiB | Larger blocks reduce requests but may over-fetch |
| `remote_hdf5_max_blocks` | 8 | More blocks retain more data per open handle |

Their product, about 40 MiB by default, approximates the memory each open handle retains. For metadata scans, reduce both, trading over-fetch for round trips; for sequential patch reads, use fewer, larger blocks. With many concurrent handles, lower `remote_hdf5_max_blocks` first. To read complete files, a local copy is usually faster than repeated range requests.

```python
with config_context(remote_hdf5_block_size=262_144, remote_hdf5_max_blocks=4):
    summaries = dc.scan_to_df([http_path])
```

HTTP and HTTPS use both settings. S3 uses its own read-ahead cache and takes the block size only.
